correctness.rationale: The geometric and first-moment series independently give w(r)=theta^2 q^(m-3)q^(-r)(r+b)/(q^m-1), q=1+theta, b=theta+2+m/(q^m-1). Neighbor ratios strictly decrease, and their difference from 1 has the sign of H_m-r. With A=theta sum(q^k), strict AM–GM gives m^2 q^(m-1)/A^2 < theta^(-2), so H'_m<-1. Expanding the finite sum gives H_m(0+)=(m-5)/2, not attained, while H_m(infinity)=-infinity. Therefore the only nonnegative integer thresholds are j<(m-5)/2. This handles m=2 (vacuous interior concavity), m=5 (endpoint limit 0 but no tie), and m=6 (first positive threshold). In all cases H_m<m-1, so there is no missing overflow sector; every claimed unique mode occurs on an interval and any tie is exactly adjacent. For m=6 clearing theta A and removing theta^2 yields the stated sextic. For the large-m transition, A/m increases strictly in m at fixed theta; t_m increases toward t_*=sqrt(2)-1 by pointwise convergence of H_m. Its positive lower bound t_6 and the mean-value theorem give t_*-t_m=O(m(1+t_6)^(-m)), so ((1+t_m)/sqrt(2))^m tends to one. The derivative of 1/t-t-2 then gives the stated limiting coefficient 1/(4+2sqrt(2)).
residual_risks: Log-concavity is on interior labeled residues, not a claim about wraparound triples. The analytic proof supplies all resolutions and all real positive parameters; fraction checks certify only the enclosure.
